what: `py -I harness/v2/agents.py` selected Python 3.9 and failed on `str | None`; the documented `uv run --frozen` command then failed because `uv` is not installed.
cost: Local agent how-to lookup and Python harness self-tests could not start.
cause: The checkout does not provide or bootstrap the Python 3.13 and uv tools that its contributor commands require.
whys: The scripts require Python 3.13; Windows resolves `py` to 3.9; no repository-local launcher installs the pinned interpreter; the documented command assumes uv is already present; therefore a fresh Windows checkout cannot run the agent or harness scripts.
class: Contributor checks whose required interpreter and runner are assumed rather than bootstrapped.
prevention: Provide one repository bootstrap entry point that installs the pinned uv and Python and runs typed scripts identically on every supported host; open.
workaround: Implement with source inspection and run the checks after uv and Python 3.13 are available.
fix: Not part of the Windows regression coverage change.
